audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 6, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for the thirty-thousand-person procession, ark title, new-cart transport, Uzzah's fatal contact, David's anger and fear, Obed-edom the Gittite, sacrifice, ecstatic dance, Michal's observation and protest, servant women, food distribution, exposure language, and childlessness.

verses.restored: David again gathered all chosen men in Israel, thirty thousand.

familiar.text: Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

verses.restored: David arose and went with all people who were with him from Baale-judah to bring up from there ark of Divine, upon which Name is called, Name of YHWH of hosts, who sits above cherubim.

familiar.text: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims.

verses.restored: They mounted ark of Divine upon a new cart and carried it from house of Abinadab, which was on hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving new cart.

familiar.text: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.

verses.restored: They carried it from house of Abinadab, which was on hill, with ark of Divine, and Ahio was walking before ark.

familiar.text: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.

verses.restored: David and all house of Israel were celebrating before YHWH with all kinds of cypress-wood instruments, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles/sistra, and cymbals.

familiar.text: And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.

verses.restored: They came to threshing floor of Nacon, and Uzzah reached toward ark of Divine and took hold of it, because cattle stumbled.

familiar.text: And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH burned against Uzzah, and Divine struck him there for the error/irreverence, and he died there beside ark of Divine.

familiar.text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.

verses.restored: David became angry because YHWH had broken out in a breach against Uzzah. That place has been called Perez-uzzah until this day.

familiar.text: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perezuzzah to this day.

verses.restored: David was afraid of YHWH on that day and said, How can ark of YHWH come to me?

familiar.text: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?

verses.restored: David was not willing to turn ark of YHWH toward himself into City of David. David turned it aside to house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

familiar.text: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.

verses.restored: Ark of YHWH stayed in house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and YHWH blessed Obed-edom and all his house.

familiar.text: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obededom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obededom, and all his household.

verses.restored: It was told to king David, saying, YHWH has blessed house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him because of ark of Divine. David went and brought up ark of Divine from house of Obed-edom to City of David with joy.

familiar.text: And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obededom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obededom into the city of David with gladness.

verses.restored: When bearers of ark of YHWH had stepped six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal.

familiar.text: And it was so, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

verses.restored: David was whirling/dancing with all his strength before YHWH, and David was girded with a linen ephod.

familiar.text: And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.

verses.restored: David and all house of Israel brought up ark of YHWH with shouting and sound of shofar.

familiar.text: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

verses.restored: As ark of YHWH came into City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down through window and saw king David leaping and whirling before YHWH, and she despised him in her heart.

familiar.text: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.

verses.restored: They brought ark of YHWH and set it in its place within tent David had pitched for it. David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before YHWH.

familiar.text: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

verses.restored: David finished offering burnt offering and peace offerings, and he blessed people in name of YHWH of hosts.

familiar.text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

verses.restored: He distributed to all people, to whole multitude of Israel, from man even to woman, to each one a loaf of bread, a portion of food/date cake, and a raisin cake. All people went, each to his house.

familiar.text: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.

verses.restored: David returned to bless his house. Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, How glorious king of Israel was today, who uncovered himself today before eyes of maidservants of his servants, as one of vulgar men shamelessly uncovers himself.

familiar.text: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

verses.restored: David said to Michal, Before YHWH—who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me leader over people of YHWH, over Israel—I celebrated before YHWH.

familiar.text: And David said unto Michal, It was before the LORD, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.

verses.restored: I will make myself still more contemptible than this and be low in my own eyes; yet with maidservants of whom you spoke, with them I will be honored.

familiar.text: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.

verses.restored: Michal daughter of Saul had no child until day of her death.

familiar.text: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.

translation_notes: Uzzah responds to a stumbling cart by stabilizing the ark and dies immediately. The chapter presents sacred violence; it must not be turned into victim-blaming, a workplace-safety slogan, or proof that accidental contact deserves death.
The transport involves a new cart, draft animals, multiple workers, musicians, and a mass procession. Religious spectacle does not remove organizational responsibility for preventable danger.
Obed-edom is identified as Gittite, likely linking a Philistine-associated identity to a household portrayed as blessed. Sacred presence crosses enemy categories.
The ark must not be treated as a magical object whose possession guarantees blessing, prosperity, political legitimacy, or protection.
Animal sacrifice and mass celebration carry material and animal costs that should not disappear beneath pageantry.

Michal watches from within the palace and objects to royal exposure before servant women. Her response may include class concern, sexual boundaries, public humiliation, dynastic trauma, or contempt; the narrator does not give a complete interior explanation.
David answers by invoking Divine choice over Michal's father and house, intensifying a marital conflict through political and theological dominance.
The servant women are discussed by both royal spouses but are given no speech. They are not props in an argument about David's authenticity.

Michal's childlessness is reported without an explicit causal statement. It may reflect infertility, separation, withheld intimacy, political confinement, or narrative closure; it must never be preached as punishment for criticizing worship.
The food distribution includes women explicitly and links celebration to material provision, though the exact food terms remain philologically uncertain.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not teach that Uzzah deserved death, that accidents reveal impure hearts, or that leaders may spiritualize unsafe systems. Do not vilify Michal or equate infertility with punishment. Protect bodily boundaries, worker safety, disabled and foreign-associated persons, servant women's dignity, and freedom from coerced religious spectacle.
